title: Lanterns Episode 3 Focuses on John Stewart
seoTitle: Lanterns Episode 3 Focuses on John Stewart
subtitle: The DC series delves into the character's journey with revelations about his childhood and training
excerpt: The third episode of Lanterns puts the spotlight on John Stewart, exploring his childhood, flashbacks, and connections to the Green Lantern Corps.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The third episode of the series Lanterns puts the spotlight on the journey of John Stewart, played by Aaron Pierre. The recent chapter serves as a deep dive into the character's backstory, dividing into three flashback storylines that reveal details about his childhood, his service with the Marines, and his interview with a Guardian of the Universe.

Family Influence and the Choice for the Corps

The plot shows how John Sr., John Stewart's father, was visited by a ring that rejected him due to fear, creating consequences and trauma within the family. Following a visit from the Guardian of the Universe, the parents decided to dedicate their younger son's life to the mission of joining the Green Lantern Corps. This process involved a strict upbringing, compared in the episode to the routine imposed on athletes by their parents, shaping a hero focused solely on the mission.

The Mystery of the Constructs and Theories About the Character

As the series moves forward with the conspiracy involving the Manhunters in the town of Rushville, John Stewart's behavior draws attention due to his unusual abilities. During a moment when he is tested by Hal Jordan, played by Kyle Chandler, John creates a bird-shaped construct that continues to exist even after the ring completely loses its charge and the user falls unconscious, sparking theories about his true nature in the story.

Connections to the Comics and the Future of the Narrative

The script also brings back classic comic book elements by showing John's time in art school, highlighting his visual creativity. Torn between the rigor of his upbringing and his artistic capabilities, the character establishes himself as the primary dramatic focus of this phase in the series' narrative.
